Let $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ be the tank's length, width, and height, respectively. We wish to minimize the function

$$
f(x,y,z)=xy+2xz+2yz,
$$

subject to the constraint 

$$
xyz=256.
$$

Note that we also have the constraints $x>0,y>0,z>0.$

Let $g(x,y,z)=xyz.$ Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z),\,g(x,y,z)=256
$$

We start by solving the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x}(x,y,z),{f}_{y}(x,y,z),{f}_{z}(x,y,z)⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x}(x,y,z),{g}_{y}(x,y,z),{g}_{z}(x,y,z)⟩ \\ ⟨y+2z,x+2z,2x+2y⟩ & =\lambda ⟨yz,xz,xy⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y+2z=\lambda yz \\ x+2z=\lambda xz \\ 2x+2y=\lambda xy\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the first, second, and third equations by $x,y,$ and $z$ respectively, we get the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x(y+2z)=\lambda xyz \\ y(x+2z)=\lambda xyz \\ z(2x+2y)=\lambda xyz\end{aligned}
$$

From the first and second equations above, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x(y+2z) & =y(x+2z) \\ xy+2xz & =xy+2yz \\ 2xz & =2yz \\ 2z(x-y) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z>0,$ we can conclude that $x=y.$

Similarly, from the second and third equations, we get that $x=y=2z.$ So, using the constraint equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}xyz & =256 \\ (2z)(2z)z & =256 \\ 4{z}^{3} & =256 \\ {z}^{3} & =64 \\ z & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is reached at the point $(8,8,4),$ and the minimum value is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(8,8,4)=8(8)+2(8)(4)+2(8)(4)=192\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** It's easy to show that the obtained point is indeed the minimum (and not the maximum). To do that, we could compare the value of the function at this point with the value of the function at any other (arbitrary) point belonging to the domain. For example, 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(16,16,1) & =(16)(16)+2(16)(1)+2(16)(1) \\  & =320 \\  & >f(8,8,4).\end{aligned}
$$
